checks: Normal/elevated/stage-one/stage-two categories and higher systolic-or-diastolic category.
Current PREVENT 7.5% risk pathway and lower-risk lifestyle trial for three to six months.
Measurement quality and out-of-office assessment.
Different elevated-pressure and diagnostic boundaries; home/awake/24-hour/sleep thresholds.
Correct cuff dimensions, preparation, timed orthostatic measurements.
White-coat versus masked phenotypes and nocturnal level versus relative dipping.
No demonstrated reduction in death or major cardiovascular events from bedtime versus morning treatment in the studied primary-care population; do not infer universal benefit from nondipping alone.
AHA PREVENT 7.5% threshold and persistent low-risk pressure after 3–6 months.
General AHA target and ESC risk-based treatment below diagnostic hypertension boundary.
ESC tolerability, symptomatic orthostasis, age 85, frailty and lifespan exceptions.
AHA baseline kidney/electrolyte, albuminuria, glycemic, lipid and ECG evaluation.
sourceChecks.retrievalNote: Current AHA society summary read directly; publisher primary documents cross-checked through indexed primary-source passages because full-page retrieval was blocked.

checks: Usual adult start 5 mg daily, selected lower start 2.5 mg and maximum 10 mg daily.

sourceChecks.source: NHLBI DASH and WHO sodium recommendations
checks: DASH food groups, calorie-dependent servings and fat quality.
WHO adult sodium <2000 mg/day and approximate 5 g/day salt equivalent.

sourceChecks.source: SSaSS primary randomized trial and ESC lifestyle recommendations
checks: 75% sodium chloride/25% potassium chloride trial intervention, selected population and hyperkalemia-related exclusions.
Exercise intensity/time alternatives, resistance training and alcohol upper limit.
Do not extrapolate salt-substitute safety to advanced CKD with existing hyperkalemia.
Broader conditional aldosterone/renin screening recommendation; biochemical screening does not imply routine adrenal imaging.

sourceChecks.source: KDIGO 2024 CKD and drug prescribing information
checks: Albuminuria-directed RAS blockade, no ACEi/ARB dual blockade, renal/potassium monitoring and >30% creatinine rise trigger.
Drug doses, adverse electrolyte effects and complementary BP-drug mechanisms.
Stage-four CKD population, ABPM outcome at 12 weeks, 12.5 mg start and maximum 50 mg/day trial escalation.
Approximately 10.5 mmHg adjusted between-group systolic difference and greater hypokalemia, creatinine increase, hyperglycemia, dizziness and hyperuricemia.
No definitive dialysis or mortality benefit established by this BP trial.
sourceChecks.retrievalNote: Publisher-hosted primary PDF retrieved; abstract and trial methods/results checked directly, including -10.5 mmHg between-group result.

checks: Adequate foundational triple regimen, pseudoresistance exclusion and diuretic optimization.
PATHWAY-2 arms, 25–50 mg spironolactone and home systolic BP endpoint.
Distinguish AHA routine MRA eGFR >=45 pathway from selected ESC eGFR >=30 and potassium <=4.5 mmol/L use.
Eplerenone indication-specific dose, renal/CYP3A limitations and potassium monitoring before treatment, within one week and at one month.
Clonidine rebound, supervised taper and sequencing when concurrent beta blockade is being discontinued.

sourceChecks.source: AHA renal-denervation statement and ACC 2026 pathway
checks: Selected adjunctive procedural role, modest variable BP lowering, ongoing medication/follow-up and no substitution of BP effects for a proven hard-outcome benefit.
American definition includes above-goal pressure despite three complementary drugs including a diuretic, or control requiring at least four.
sourceChecks.retrievalNote: AHA society statement summary retrieved directly. Indexed ACC 2026 primary passages checked for definition and MRA priority; full pathway review remains part of final chapter review.

checks: Conditional wider screening and normokalemic presentations.
Assay-specific aldosterone thresholds, suppressed-renin framework, PRA-based ARR cutoff and unit limits.
Potassium/medication confounders and clinically safe repeat-testing strategies.
Overt phenotype exception to suppression testing, CT/AVS roles and young-patient exception.
Uncontrolled BP with suppressed renin as a reason to titrate tolerated MRA therapy; uncertainty when BP is already controlled.
sourceChecks.retrievalNote: Society recommendation page retrieved directly and relevant recommendations read. Full publisher page redirected to an inaccessible CDN; no claim of full journal-text review.

sourceChecks.source: AHA renal revascularization statement and CORAL
checks: No routine clinical-event benefit for stenting in the studied CORAL population.
Recurrent flash pulmonary edema as a selective revascularization-review phenotype; observational evidence limits.
Lesion-significance framework: >70% narrowing, mean gradient >10 mmHg or renal FFR <0.8, with a compatible clinical syndrome.
Renal FMD angioplasty without routine stenting; selected bailout or surgical circumstances.

sourceChecks.source: AASM OSA testing guidance and HIPARCO
checks: PSG after a negative/inconclusive/inadequate home study when clinical suspicion persists.
Settings favoring initial PSG and generally modest, adherence-dependent BP response to CPAP.
Do not misstate the HIPARCO 24-hour mean BP/DBP effects as a statistically significant SBP result.
Establish alpha blockade before adding beta blockade; typical 7–14-day preparation and individualized volume management.
Doxazosin starting-dose range and amiloride 5-mg starting-dose information checked.

sourceChecks.source: Liddle genotype/phenotype primary data and aortic/ACHD guidance
checks: ENaC gain-of-function, suppressed renin/aldosterone, variable phenotype and ENaC-directed treatment.
Arm/leg pressure and pulse localization, cross-sectional aortic imaging, associated disease and continued follow-up.
Do not equate Doppler peak instantaneous and invasive peak-to-peak gradients.
Acute organ injury defines emergency; stable chronic changes and an isolated number do not suffice.
General recommendation is no more than 25% SBP reduction in hour one, then <160/100 in 2–6 hours and cautious further reduction over 24–48 hours.
Do not automatically transfer a MAP formulation to the quoted 2025 SBP wording.
No intermittent IV/oral rescue dosing for asymptomatic noncardiac inpatients solely to acutely lower severe pressure.
Nicardipine 5 mg/h, 2.5-mg/h increments and 15-mg/h maximum; drug selection considers bradycardia, bronchospasm, renal and neurological context.
sourceChecks.retrievalNote: Primary guideline indexed recommendations cross-checked; no claim of unrestricted full publisher retrieval.

sourceChecks.source: ISTH TTP guidance and Catalan expert protocol
checks: High-probability TTP warrants urgent plasma exchange/corticosteroids after pretreatment ADAMTS13 sampling; severe hypertension does not exclude TTP.
PLASMIC components and risk bands; ADAMTS13 <10% threshold.
Specific expert protocol example: 1–1.5 plasma volumes and IV methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg after exchange; do not present variable protocols as a single universal ISTH dose.
2025 immune-TTP treatment recommendations retained; congenital-TTP ADAMTS13 prevention is a separate indication.

sourceChecks.source: Acute aortic, coronary and pulmonary-pressure management
checks: Acute aortic anti-impulse sequence; HR 60–80/min and SBP <120 or lowest perfusion-preserving pressure.
Esmolol 500 microgram/kg load and 50 microgram/kg/min starting infusion checked against prescribing information.
Pulmonary edema can reflect afterload-driven redistribution despite preserved EF and no large weight gain.
Nitrate infusion ranges and early NIV/volume assessment; do not claim a universal high-dose bolus requirement.
Coronary perfusion gradient depends on aortic diastolic pressure and LV filling pressure.

sourceChecks.source: AHA 2025 ICH recommendation and AHA/ASA stroke guidance
checks: 2025 hypertension guidance selected ICH range 130 to <140; distinguish the 2022 ICH 140 target with 130–150 maintenance range.
Before IVT: SBP <185 AND DBP <110; after IVT: <180/105 for at least 24 hours.

2026 guidance: no functional benefit from intensive <140 after IVT in the stated population; active target <140 for 72 hours after successful anterior-circulation EVT is harmful without another indication.

sourceChecks.source: ASAM/AAAP guideline and NHS injectable diazepam protocol
checks: Benzodiazepines first-line for stimulant-associated hyperadrenergic agitation; add syndrome-directed short-acting agents when needed.
Avoid an unqualified all-beta-blockers prohibition; selected combined alpha/beta blockade is discussed in contemporary guidance.
NHS v3 symptomatic cocaine protocol example: 1–2 mg slow IV increments over 2 minutes, 2–5-minute intervals, titration toward 10 mg, possible further dose after 10 minutes, 20-mg episode ceiling.
sourceChecks.retrievalNote: Public NHS Word attachment retrieved in memory because the web parser does not support DOCX. Dose table and off-label status read directly; no source document copied into the repository.

checks: Persistent >=160 systolic or >=110 diastolic over about 15 minutes; urgent treatment within 30–60 minutes of confirmation.
Rapid labetalol/hydralazine/oral IR nifedipine versus the separate magnesium seizure-prevention indication.
SOMANZ example: 4 g magnesium over 20 minutes then 1 g/hour; continue 24 hours after delivery or last seizure, whichever later; renal/respiratory/reflex monitoring and calcium rescue.
Nifedipine ER 30–120 mg/day for maintenance; asthma can favor it over labetalol.
CHAP-informed initiation/titration at 140/90; avoid ARBs in pregnancy.

sourceChecks.source: SPRINT, ACCORD-BP, BPROAD, STEP and HYVET primary evidence
checks: SPRINT age/risk eligibility, diabetes/stroke exclusions, original 2015 HRs 0.75/0.73 and selected adverse-event excess.
ACCORD-BP primary HR 0.88 (nonsignificant) versus stroke HR 0.59; do not equate a nonsignificant test with equivalence.
BPROAD diabetic population, age >=50, eGFR <30 exclusion, full endpoint including treated/hospitalized HF, HR 0.79 and specific safety signals.
STEP ages 60–80 and bounded targets 110–<130 versus 130–<150, HR 0.74.
HYVET selected age >=80/SBP >=160, indapamide SR 1.5 mg plus optional perindopril 2–4 mg; final stroke P=0.06, mortality/HF benefit; no substitution of interim results.
sourceChecks.retrievalNote: Primary trial abstracts/indexed publisher text, primary protocol/cohort papers and current society guidance cross-checked; publisher full-page retrieval was restricted for several articles.

limitations: Source checks are author verification, not independent clinician review.
Structural validation does not establish completeness or clinical accuracy.

finalDetailReview.result: ESC 2024 minimum 70% usable readings, typically >=27 over 24 h, with time-distribution and diary limitations included.
Named ESC/ESH voltage cutoffs, poor sensitivity and role of directed echocardiography included; source uses >35 mm rather than silently treating the source DOCX >= convention as identical.
Surgery-risk and timing qualifications, selected RAS-inhibitor omission, HFrEF continuation and established beta-blocker continuation included.

All three distractors individually explained; full four-grade table included.
